problem: Offline reinforcement learning with trajectory preferences struggles to learn robust policies when data coverage is poor and lacks algorithmic tractability or theoretical guarantees.
approach: MCP leverages a tractable conservative learning framework that improves policies upon a reference policy supported by the data, using a general function class without requiring known transition dynamics.
contribution: First provably sample-efficient and computationally tractable offline preference-based RL algorithm under partial data coverage.

problem: Large Language Models struggle to understand molecular graphs effectively because existing graph-LLM bridges use fixed-length static tokens that overlook stereochemistry and substructural context.
approach: EDT-Former generates tokens aligned with informative molecular patches using entropy-guided dynamic token selection, enabling frozen graph encoders to align with LLMs without backbone fine-tuning.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results on MoleculeQA, Mol-Instructions, and property prediction benchmarks with efficient multimodal molecular understanding.

problem: Multi-view 3D reconstruction methods fail when input views have insufficient overlap, occlusions, or sparse coverage, resulting in incomplete reconstructions.
approach: ReconViaGen integrates reconstruction priors into a diffusion-based generative framework with cross-view connections and improved denoising controllability to generate consistent plausible structures.
contribution: Reconstructs complete and accurate 3D models consistent with input views in both global structure and local details despite sparse view coverage.

problem: No large-scale benchmark exists for evaluating LLM agents on complex future prediction tasks requiring real-time updates and handling data contamination.
approach: FutureX is a dynamic live benchmark with real-time daily updates, automated question/answer collection, and evaluation of 25 LLM/agent models including reasoning and search capabilities.
contribution: Establishes largest and most diverse live benchmark for future prediction with contamination-free evaluation through automated pipeline.

problem: N-gram novelty alone is an inadequate metric for textual creativity because it ignores creativity's dual nature: novelty and appropriateness.
approach: Study the relationship between n-gram novelty and expert-judged creativity through 7542 annotations of human and AI-generated text via close reading.
contribution: Demonstrates that ~91% of top-quartile n-gram novel expressions are not judged as creative, showing n-gram novelty correlates with lower pragmaticality in LLMs.

problem: Existing unlearning methods for LLMs remain vulnerable to relearning during subsequent training, allowing forgotten knowledge to resurface.
approach: Ssiuu employs attribution-guided regularization to prevent spurious negative influence and faithfully remove target knowledge instead of hiding it.
contribution: Reliably erases target knowledge and outperforms baselines across adversarial injection and instruction-following retraining scenarios.

problem: Driving world models evaluate generation quality but overlook downstream perception performance, and synthetic data benefits disappear when training epochs are equalized.
approach: Dream4Drive decomposes video into 3D-aware guidance maps and renders 3D assets onto them, enabling fine-tuned world models to produce multi-view photorealistic videos for training perception models.
contribution: Generates multi-view corner cases at scale that significantly boost corner case perception in autonomous driving.

problem: Existing language agent benchmarks focus on narrow domains or simplified tasks lacking the diversity, realism, and long-horizon complexity of real-world applications.
approach: Toolathlon provides 32 software applications, 604 tools from MCP servers, realistic environment states from real software, and 108 manually sourced tasks requiring ~20 interaction turns.
contribution: Largest and most diverse benchmark for language agents with reliable execution-based evaluation across real-world applications.

problem: The LLM community focuses almost exclusively on decoder-only models while lacking fair comparisons between encoder-only and decoder-only architectures trained with identical recipes.
approach: Ettin suite provides paired encoder-only and decoder-only models (17M to 1B params) trained on up to 2 trillion tokens with the same recipe.
contribution: Beats ModernBERT as encoder and Llama 3.2 and SmolLM2 as decoders; shows encoder tasks benefit from encoders while decoders excel at generation.

problem: LLMs' autoregressive decoding limits their ability to revisit and refine earlier tokens holistically, leading to inefficient exploration of diverse solutions.
approach: LaDiR unifies continuous latent representations with latent diffusion by encoding reasoning steps into VAE latent blocks and denoising them with blockwise bidirectional attention.
contribution: Consistently improves accuracy, diversity, and interpretability on mathematical reasoning and planning benchmarks over autoregressive and existing diffusion methods.

problem: LLMs applied to forecasting tasks may fail evaluation due to temporal leakage and unclear generalization to real-world forecasting performance.
approach: Systematic analysis identifies two categories of evaluation issues: temporal leakage and failure to extrapolate from evaluation to real-world forecasting.
contribution: Demonstrates through concrete examples how evaluation flaws can invalidate current performance claims about LLM forecasting abilities.

problem: Existing equivariant policy learning methods require structured inputs like 3D point clouds or top-down views, preventing their use in low-cost or dynamic environments.
approach: RAVEN is the first SE(3)-equivariant policy framework operating on RGB images by treating image data as collections of rays that transform under 3D roto-translations.
contribution: Consistently surpasses baselines in both performance and efficiency on robot manipulation in simulation and real-world settings.

problem: State-of-the-art 3D occupancy estimation methods rely on slow voxel-based or dense Gaussian representations lacking flexibility for temporal dynamics.
approach: S2GO summarizes scenes into compact query sets propagated through time online, decoded into semantic Gaussians at each timestep with denoising rendering.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on nuScenes and KITTI occupancy benchmarks with 4.5x faster inference than GaussianWorld.

problem: It is unclear when Transformers can learn to rely on causal features instead of spurious correlations, especially under strong data correlation.
approach: Analyzes Transformer training through correlation strength and implicit regularization, identifying Correlation Crowding-Out where gradient descent filters spurious cues.
contribution: Shows that under suitable conditions, standard training induces cause-only prediction through occupation and crowding-out mechanisms.

problem: Diffusion-based image generation suffers from slow inference due to computational expense, and prior caching methods use rigid heuristics with limited generalization.
approach: ECAD uses a genetic algorithm to learn efficient per-model caching schedules forming a Pareto frontier from calibration prompts, with no network modifications required.
contribution: Achieves significant inference speedups with fine-grained quality-latency trade-off control, generalizing to unseen resolutions and model variants.

problem: Symbolic regression truncates the scientific discovery cycle by focusing on hypothesis and experiment without systematic analysis of structural errors.
approach: RESTART closes the loop with a principled analysis stage: short-term refinement uses boosting to identify unexplained signals, long-term library distills successful refinements.
contribution: Achieves lower error and higher accuracy than baselines on LLM-SRBench; recovers near-exact functional forms on out-of-distribution data.

problem: Static classifier-free guidance scales fail to adapt to diverse prompt requirements in text-to-image diffusion, and existing solutions introduce complexity without generalization.
approach: Dynamic CFG scheduling leverages online feedback from small-scale latent-space evaluators (CLIP, discriminator, reward model) to select optimal per-timestep guidance scales.
contribution: Achieves up to 53.8% human preference win-rate vs default Imagen 3 baseline with improvements in text alignment, visual quality, and text rendering.

problem: Neural datasets contain heterogeneous populations of stable and stochastic cells, making it hard to identify consistent activity patterns during self-supervised pretraining.
approach: POYO-SSL exploits heterogeneity by pretraining only on predictable neurons identified via skewness and kurtosis, then fine-tuning on unpredictable population.
contribution: Yields 12-13% relative gains over from-scratch training with smooth monotonic scaling on Allen Brain Observatory; exhibits no plateau as model size increases.

problem: Video understanding in multimodal LMs is limited by context length, causing missed key frames and poor coherence across long time scales.
approach: VideoNSA adapts Native Sparse Attention to video-LMs via end-to-end training on 216K video instruction dataset with hardware-aware hybrid attention strategy.
contribution: Reliably scales to 128K tokens with improved long-video understanding, temporal reasoning, and spatial performance over token-compression baselines.

problem: AdamW is the default optimizer for transformer pretraining but the community has struggled to find faster, more stable alternatives.
approach: Single-line modification to any momentum-based optimizer creates cautious optimizers (C-AdamW, C-Lion) that preserve Adam's Hamiltonian and convergence guarantees.
contribution: Consistent speed-up on LLM pretraining and post-training with better results on MAE pretraining and minimal hyperparameter tuning required.

problem: Diffusion LLMs introduce unprecedented vulnerabilities distinct from autoregressive LLMs due to iterative and parallel generation mechanisms.
approach: DiffuGuard uses stochastic annealing remasking to mitigate greedy selection bias and block-level audit-repair that exploits internal representations for risk detection.
contribution: Reduces attack success rate from 47.9% to 14.7% across six jailbreak methods while preserving model utility and efficiency.

problem: Recent hardware-accelerated FP4 formats (MXFP4, NVFP4) promise efficiency gains but their practical benefits remain unproven due to format-specific challenges.
approach: MR-GPTQ tailors GPTQ quantization to FP4 using block-wise Hadamard transforms and format-specific optimizations supported by high-performance GPU kernels.
contribution: Achieves speedups up to 3.6x layer-wise on NVIDIA B200 and 6x on RTX5090 with accuracy matching or outperforming state-of-the-art.

problem: Vision-language model evaluation relies mainly on English benchmarks and translations of English datasets that fail to capture cultural nuances.
approach: Kaleidoscope is a large-scale in-language benchmark covering 18 languages and 14 subjects with 20,911 multiple-choice questions built through open science collaboration.
contribution: Demonstrates that multilingual VLMs perform poorly on low-resource languages and complex multimodal scenarios, highlighting need for culturally inclusive evaluation.

problem: Continual learning suffers from catastrophic forgetting; existing approaches like replay and EWC have limitations in data generation and task optimization.
approach: Leverages rank-1 Fisher structure of diffusion models to propose rank-1 EWC variant paired with replay for parameter sharing while mitigating drift.
contribution: Consistently improves average FID and reduces forgetting; nearly eliminates on MNIST/FashionMNIST and roughly halves on ImageNet-1k.

problem: Cache-affinity scheduling for KV cache reuse conflicts with load-balancing requirements in distributed LLM serving, forcing suboptimal routing choices.
approach: DualMap maps each request to two candidate instances using independent hash functions, then intelligently selects the better candidate based on system state.
contribution: Simultaneously enables cache affinity and load balancing with SLO-aware routing and hotspot-aware rebalancing for dynamic workloads.

problem: Conformal prediction relies on softmax-derived nonconformity scores that unreliably indicate model certainty, limiting prediction set adaptiveness.
approach: Leverages Helmholtz Free Energy as uncertainty measure and reweights nonconformity scores with monotonic transformation of energy score for each sample.
contribution: Improves adaptiveness of prediction sets with notable increase in both efficiency and adaptiveness compared to baseline nonconformity scores.

problem: In-context learning is effective but incurs high inference costs as context length grows, limiting practical applications.
approach: Prompt-MII uses RL-based framework to meta-learn instruction induction that reduces training examples to compact descriptive prompts achieving comparable ICL performance.
contribution: Improves downstream model quality by 4-9 F1 points while requiring 3-13x fewer tokens, trained on 3,000+ diverse classification datasets.

problem: Evaluating diffusion posterior sampling algorithms lacks distribution-level comparisons and gold-standard reference methods for inverse problems.
approach: Proposes statistical benchmark using discretized Lévy processes with efficient Gibbs sampling methods that provide gold-standard posterior samples for DPS evaluation.
contribution: Enables arbitrary-precision Monte Carlo estimation and isolation of algorithmic errors from learned component errors across multiple inverse problems.

problem: Semantic caches using static similarity thresholds lack formal correctness guarantees, resulting in unexpected error rates and suboptimal cache hit rates.
approach: vCache employs online learning algorithm to estimate optimal threshold for each cached prompt, enabling reliable cache responses with user-defined error bounds.
contribution: Consistently meets specified error bounds while achieving up to 12.5x higher cache hit and 26x lower error rates vs static-threshold baselines.

problem: Text-image manipulation methods struggle with text removal, lack style control, and tend to generate duplicated letters despite advances in inpainting.
approach: OmniText leverages cross- and self-attention mechanisms to enable text removal via inversion and style control via redistributed attention, using latent optimization.
contribution: Training-free generalist for diverse text image manipulation tasks with novel loss functions and OmniText-Bench dataset for evaluation.

problem: Generative classifiers using diffusion-based approaches suffer from substantial computational costs, limiting scalability for practical applications.
approach: Investigates VAR-based generative classifiers which offer tractable likelihood, proposes Adaptive VAR Classifier+ for improved accuracy and efficiency.
contribution: Achieves significantly more efficient inference than diffusion-based counterparts with improved accuracy; enables visual explainability via token-wise mutual information.

problem: RL-based scaling approaches for tool use struggle to scale thinking length sufficiently for complex problems and waste tokens on simple problems through overthinking.
approach: Uses warm-up supervised fine-tuning to distinguish simple/complex problems, then applies entropy-based optimization objectives to enable automatic reasoning-length scaling.
contribution: Achieves auto-scaling for efficient tool use with 9.8% accuracy improvements while reducing computational overhead by ~81%.

problem: Existing navigation models struggle to provide unified solutions across heterogeneous paradigms like instruct-goal, object-goal, point-goal navigation, and exploration.
approach: OmniNav proposes fast-slow system design: fast module generates waypoints from short-horizon context, slow module conducts deliberative planning over long-horizon observations.
contribution: Handles multiple navigation paradigms within single architecture with high precision waypoint prediction supporting real-world deployment up to 5 Hz.

problem: Conventional RNNs collapse temporal dynamics into fixed-dimensional hidden states, limiting adaptability and context learning for sequence modeling.
approach: WARP parametrizes hidden state as weights and biases of auxiliary network driven by input differences, enabling gradient-free test-time adaptation and physics-informed priors.
contribution: Matches or surpasses state-of-the-art on diverse tasks; physics-informed variant outperforms baseline by >10x on dynamical system reconstruction.

problem: LLMs perform multi-step reasoning but cannot reliably verify their own logic, with flawed reasoning undermining trust in high-stakes scenarios.
approach: VeriCoT extracts formal logical arguments from CoT, formalizes steps into first-order logic, identifies premises, and uses automated solvers to verify validity.
contribution: Effectively identifies flawed reasoning and serves as strong predictor of answer correctness; improves reasoning via self-reflection and preference fine-tuning.

problem: LLMs have limited parametric knowledge and existing RAGs struggle with knowledge-intensive tasks due to fragmented information and weak graph structure modeling.
approach: G-reasoner integrates graph and language foundation models with QuadGraph, a standardized four-layer abstraction unifying heterogeneous knowledge into common representation.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on six benchmarks with scalable 34M-parameter graph foundation model integrated with LLMs.

problem: MLLMs often struggle with fine-grained visual understanding and hallucinations due to over-reliance on linguistic priors that distract from actual visual information.
approach: MMGrounded-PostAlign introduces dual grounding with visual module identifying referred objects and textual module generating rationale, plus negative rejection and selective reasoning.
contribution: Significant improvements on POPE, HaloQuest, ReasonSeg, MME, and MMBench benchmarks with enhanced visual-textual alignment and reduced hallucinations.

problem: Existing variance-dependent lower bounds for linear contextual bandits have gaps with upper bounds and only consider fixed total variance budgets, not general variance sequences.
approach: Establishes variance-dependent lower bounds for both prefixed and adaptive variance sequences using novel analysis techniques.
contribution: Overcomes limitations of prior work with improved lower bound of Ω(d√(Σσ²_k)/log K) that closes gap with existing upper bounds.

problem: Diffusion-based image compositing struggles to preserve coherent spatial relations in pairwise or sequential edits, with subsequent insertions overwriting previous content.
approach: PICS uses self-supervised composition-by-decomposition with Interaction Transformer employing Mixture-of-Experts and adaptive α-blending for compatibility-aware fusion.
contribution: Delivers superior pairwise compositing quality and substantially improved stability across virtual try-on, indoor, and street scene settings.

problem: Weighting methods in federated learning operate efficiently but fail to address the main obstacle: communication bottleneck in heterogeneous data scenarios.
approach: Incorporates compression into the weighting scheme with convergence analysis under convexity for both exact and stochastic oracles.
contribution: Establishes convergence guarantees while addressing communication bottleneck in federated learning with heterogeneous data.
